answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making every new identity earn reputation through verifiable work before it can transact at full value. A fresh agent starts with a small trust budget, like an opal whose worth is only revealed after it is cut and tested. To forge a trusted identity it must complete many low-value, attested tasks over time, while a saffron-priced stake — expensive to replicate at scale — is locked and slashed on fraud. Copying identities then costs more than it gains.
